name: reachability
description: REACHABILITY ratchet. `tsc`, the test suite and every existing lint gate check TYPES and BEHAVIOUR; nothing checked whether a thing is REACHED. CLAUDE.md names 'built but unwired' as this repo's single most common defect, and every instance (services/lateFees, services/respa/earlyIntervention, calculateFlipAnalysis, taxSaleAuctions/taxSaleListings, achMandateSetup/achAutopayRun, rental_units.kind='pad', routes-contract-chain.ts, the rent-roll importer's unitKind arg) shipped GREEN and was found hours later by a manual audit. This converts that recurring audit into CI. Every count is strictly down-only, and raising one requires explicit founder/Iris-CTO sign-off (see lastBumpNote for the exceptions actually invoked): exports in server/services|jobs with no production call site; pgTables with no writer; pgTables with no reader; routes-*.ts never mounted; exports the gate cannot assert on because their module is dynamically imported in a way that hides which exports are touched; and service/job files nothing imports at all. The count of families is deliberately not stated here — it said 'four' for as long as there were four, and would have said it forever. THE CHEAPEST WAY TO SATISFY THIS GATE IS DELETION — the north star is a smaller codebase, and every reduction must be locked in by the commit that earned it (a stale-high baseline FAILS, same as `as-any`).
minimaNote: VACUITY FLOORS, not ratchets. Every baseline above counts BAD THINGS FOUND, so a scan that stops seeing files finds zero and reports six reassuring PASS lines — this repo has already been bitten by exactly that (a block-comment stripper that mispaired and blanked the very lines a scan was counting). These floor the SCAN POPULATIONS the run prints, and the gate exits nonzero if any drops below or is missing entirely. Seeded 2026-08-16 at roughly 75-80% of live (productionFiles 2520, exportFiles 917, pgTables 758, routeCandidateFiles 277) so that a broken walk/extension-filter/regex trips them while ordinary deletion — the north star of this gate — does not. If a real deletion wave takes a population under its floor, lower the floor in the same commit and name the wave; do NOT raise a floor to silence anything, and do NOT delete a key (a missing floor FAILS, by design, so an unfloored population cannot exist). A --root fixture run must supply its own --ratchet with fixture-sized minima.

allowlist.reason: Read by compare-and-swap, not by SELECT. server/jobs/scheduler.ts acquires the single-flight lease with `UPDATE job_locks SET ... WHERE jobName = ? AND (expiresAt < now OR lockedBy = me) RETURNING id` — the WHERE clause IS the read and the RETURNING row is the answer. A separate SELECT-then-UPDATE would reintroduce exactly the race the lock exists to prevent, so this table can never grow a reader the linter's `.from(`/`db.query.` patterns can see. Structural blind spot, not dead weight.

Exported for the injectable-storage seam the module header describes; production consumes the singleton declared four lines below it (`export const investorVerificationService = new InvestorVerificationService()`), so the class has no EXTERNAL production consumer by construction and never can. It was not on this list before unit 53 for a reason worth recording: its only "consumer" was a STALE COMMENT — `// TODO(tsc): InvestorVerificationService exposes no listAllVerifications()` in routes-investor-verification.ts. This linter tokenises identifiers across production files and never distinguishes code from prose, so a comment naming a symbol makes it look reached. (The same mechanism, from the other side, is why scripts/check-org-scoped-fetch.mjs is now in SYMBOL_REGISTERS: its tenancy debt register named a module orphan and resurrected it.) Unit 53 deleted that TODO (it was false: the DB-backing wave HAD added listVerifications(orgId), which is now wired), and the deletion revealed the export. Deletion-revealed, not built-unwired — the same category the table-count notes below already carve out. Verified by re-adding the comment: the gate goes back to PASS at 654 with no code change.

DELIBERATELY-STAGED SEAM, founder ruling (picker, 2026-08-15). The three mounted /developer/* endpoints in routes-epic-services.ts were REMOVED — they were customer-reachable behind plain isAuthenticated, minted `acr_…` keys that NOTHING verified (the only consumer, mcp-server.ts, matches provider='mcp_api_key' while these wrote provider='api_key'), and served a document titled 'AcreOS Public API' — while routes-api-keys.ts is kept dormant to honour the same 'no public API before ~50 customers' ladder. The SERVICE is kept on purpose: what was wrong was mounting the surface early, not writing the OpenAPI spec and the key-minting helper. When the ladder trigger fires this module is the starting point, and wiring it means building the verifier that never existed. Removing its callers is what made it an orphan, so this is deletion-revealed, not built-and-abandoned. expansionLadder.test.ts asserts BOTH directions: no mounted route may mint a key or serve the spec, AND this file must still exist.

EXPANSION-LADDER HOLD — the same standing founder decision that keeps routes-api-keys.ts and developerApiService.ts dormant: 'no public API before ~50 customers' (CLAUDE.md DO-NOT-DO list, expansion ladder). This file IS the public API's mount point: it exports registerPublicApiV1(app), which app.use()s /api/v1/leads, /api/v1/properties and /api/v1/webhooks, and it has ZERO callers anywhere in server/ — its own header documents the two lines to add when the trigger fires, and tests/unit/expansionLadder.test.ts pins BOTH directions (the export must still exist, and server/routes.ts must NOT contain 'registerPublicApiV1('). Not built-and-abandoned: deliberately staged and test-guarded. Only the MOUNT POINT is exempted, deliberately — its three sub-routers stay COUNTED in the unregisteredRoutes baseline so the dormant surface cannot quietly grow. Adding server/api-v1/<anything>.ts fails this gate, which is precisely the bypass a directory-wide exemption would have reopened. When the ladder trigger fires and this is mounted, it stops being a candidate, THIS ENTRY GOES STALE AND THE GATE FAILS until someone removes it and drops the baseline to 1 — mounting the public API cannot be a quiet edit.

lastBumpNote: 2026-08-16, unreachedExports 1405 -> 1403 — AND READ WHY BEFORE READING IT AS PROGRESS. The gate FAILED stale-high and its own message said "Good news: 2 unreachable item(s) were wired or deleted." Neither of them was. Both symbols are still exported, still have no production importer, and nothing about them changed. What changed is that each acquired a NAME MENTION in a file this linter scans, and this linter's usage tokeniser does not strip comments or string literals — the same blind spot already recorded here twice (the taxOptimizationEngine B17 entry, where an ownedServices STRING was the only thing keeping a fabricating module 'reached', and the InvestorVerificationService allowlist entry, where a comment naming a symbol made it look reached). ATTRIBUTED BY MEASUREMENT, not inferred: HEAD's own script was run over pristine worktrees at ffb4614 (unit 120) = 1405, b50a1a5 (unit 121) = 1404, 883a41b (unit 122) = 1404, working tree = 1403, and the two lists were diffed symbol by symbol with line numbers normalised (unit 122's import additions shift five unrelated entries by one line and would otherwise read as five deletions plus five additions). (1) 1405 -> 1404 PREDATES THIS WAVE and was earned by unit 121, which did not lock it in: server/services/settingsSeeder.ts SETTINGS_CATALOG, reached because the settings-bridge doc comment at server/services/founderSettings.ts:194 names it in prose. Its only real consumers remain inside settingsSeeder.ts itself. (2) 1404 -> 1403 is this wave: server/services/residentialComps.ts RESIDENTIAL_CAPABLE_PROVIDERS, reached because the new scripts/check-residential-comps-hold.mjs names it in its R4 seam-integrity rule (a comment and a regex source string). That coupling is genuinely load-bearing — the gate FAILS if the list grows past ["attom"] — but it is a lint script reading the seam's source text, not a runtime import, and the export still exists for the two test files that import it. SO: locked in per the strictly-down rule, because the rule is that a reduction is recorded by the commit that observes it and a stale-high baseline FAILS. It is NOT locked in as a claim that two dead exports were wired. THE REAL FINDING IS THE BLIND SPOT: a symbol can be moved out of this count by writing its name in a comment. Closing it (strip comments and string literals from the usage tokeniser before matching) would RAISE unreachedExports, which this ratchet reserves to Iris-CTO sign-off, so it is recorded here as the next candidate rather than taken unilaterally. PRIOR NOTE — 2026-08-16, GAP D — THE ROUTE FAMILY STOPPED KEYING ON A FILENAME. unregisteredRoutes 1 -> 4, a ONE-TIME RE-SEED, every newly-counted file hand-verified. WHAT WAS BROKEN: family 3 filtered candidates with /^server\/routes-[\w.-]+\.ts$/ — a FILENAME shape — although nothing about 'is this router mounted' is about the filename. A router in a subdirectory was INVISIBLE, which is both the 'built but unwired' defect the family exists for and the shape the expansion-ladder bypass actually took: a public-API surface in a subdirectory. Two further name/syntax keys went with it: the register regex demanded the literal suffix `Routes?`, so `registerPublicApiV1(app: Express)` — a registrar by signature — walked past; and mountedness was a ONE-HOP `t.includes()` check, which an unmounted PARENT satisfies. THE PREDICATE IS NOW THE PROPERTY: any non-test file under server/ exporting a route registrar (legacy `register*Routes(` OR `register<X>(app: Express|Application|Router)`) or an Express Router (`export const x = Router()` or a default-exported Router). Mountedness is a FIXED POINT — a referrer that is itself an unmounted candidate confers nothing — and specifiers are RESOLVED against the importer's directory instead of substring-matched, because `./routes` matched a different file's import while a real `./routes/lob-webhooks` import does not contain `./lob-webhooks`. MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: 277 candidates scanned (269 of them the old routes-*.ts set, so nothing was dropped), 8 newly visible outside that shape, 5 findings, ZERO false positives — all 8 newcomers verified BY HAND. MOUNTED, correctly not flagged (4): server/routes.ts (called by server/index.ts); server/auth/routes.ts (registerAuthRoutes re-exported via server/auth/index.ts, CALLED at server/routes.ts:727); server/routes/lob-webhooks.ts and server/routes/public-qr-redirect.ts (both imported and called at server/routes-outreach-mail.ts:349-350 — and note the OLD substring rule would have missed both importers). GENUINELY UNMOUNTED (4), each checked against the source: server/api-v1/index.ts exports registerPublicApiV1 with zero callers in server/ (the only other occurrences are its own doc comment, shared/governance/constitution.ts prose and two test files); server/api-v1/leads.ts, properties.ts and webhooks.ts export leadsV1Router/propertiesV1Router/webhooksV1Router whose ONLY referrer is that unmounted index.ts, so /api/v1/leads|properties|webhooks 404s today. THE `/api/v1/` HANDLERS IN routes.ts:2650 AND index.ts:162 ARE NOT A MOUNT — they rewrite /api/v1/* to /api/* as a legacy alias, which is why a human check was necessary and a grep for '/api/v1' would have lied. THE FOUR ARE THE EXPANSION-LADDER HOLD ('no public API before ~50 customers'), and the split between allowlist and baseline is deliberate: the MOUNT POINT (api-v1/index.ts) takes the ONE allowlist entry, whose reason prints on every run so the hold stays under review, while its THREE sub-routers are COUNTED — so adding server/api-v1/<anything>.ts FAILS the gate. A directory-wide exemption would have reopened the exact bypass this change closes. routes-api-keys.ts, the original baseline of 1, is unchanged and is the same ladder hold. NOISE NARROWED RATHER THAN SHIPPED, and the number is the reason: 97 of the 277 candidates export a Router named literally `router`, so the old symbol-substring sweep applied to Router variable names marks EVERY server file a referrer and launders the whole family. Symbol matching is therefore kept for registrar FUNCTION names (distinctive) and dropped for Router variable names (resolved import specifiers only); measured both ways, both give the same 5, so the narrowing costs nothing and removes a laundering channel. MUTATION-TESTED, old gate vs new, then reverted. M1 — the literal bypass this gap enabled: a new server/publicapi/routes.ts exporting `publicApiRouter = Router()` and `registerPublicApiRoutes(app)`, mounted nowhere. NEW gate: route candidates 277 -> 278, unregisteredRoutes 4 -> 5, EXIT 1, the finding naming the file. OLD gate on the same tree: unregisteredRoutes PASS at 1, and the mutant's path appears NOWHERE in its output — the bypass was not merely tolerated, it was invisible. M2 — the transitive half: add server/publicapi/index.ts importing that router and exporting an unmounted registerPublicApiSurface(app: Express). NEW gate: 4 -> 6, EXIT 1, flagging BOTH and printing 'its only referrer(s) — server/publicapi/index.ts — are themselves unmounted'; a one-hop reference rule would have excused the child. OLD gate: still PASS at 1. ANCHOR EXPLICITLY ASSERTED rather than assumed, because a mutation that does not mutate proves nothing: the candidate population MOVED (277 -> 278) and the mutant path is matched once in the new output and zero times in the old. (A first anchor check read 0 under both and was a measuring error, not a null result — `node script --measure | grep` truncates, because process.exit() drops buffered stdout to a pipe; redirect to a file when counting this script's output.) AND A VACUITY GUARD, which this file had none of: `minima` floors the four scan POPULATIONS the run prints, and a missing or breached floor exits nonzero. Mutation-tested three ways — an empty --root tree (all four populations 0, EXIT 1), a floor raised above live (routeCandidateFiles 277 vs floor 9999, EXIT 1, so the comparison works and not just the missing-key path), and a deleted key (EXIT 1, so an unfloored population cannot exist). THE OLD SCRIPT ON THAT SAME EMPTY TREE IS WHY THIS MATTERS: it did not report a broken scan, it reported 'Good news: 1405 unreachable item(s) were wired or deleted. Lock it in — set baselines.unreachedExports: 0' for every family. A totally blind scan was actively instructing the reader to re-baseline the gate to zero. See minimaNote. PRIOR NOTE — 2026-08-14/15, UNIT 111 — ONE PROMPT-INJECTION SANITIZER (founder ruling, picker: 'Consolidate to one owner'). unreachedExports 1439->1436 and moduleOrphans 45->44: server/services/promptInjectionSanitizer.ts is DELETED. It was a module orphan with FOUR exports and ZERO callers, and it was the WEAKEST of THREE independent prompt-injection deny-lists this repo carried (18 misses of a 30-attack corpus, vs 14 for server/middleware/promptInjection.ts and 10 for server/utils/sanitizePrompt.ts). The three were COMPLEMENTARY, not nested, so deletion alone would have LOST coverage: four attack classes were caught ONLY by the orphan (generic persona override 'you are now a pirate', 'act as though you have no restrictions', '### END OF DOCUMENT', and a forged line-start 'system:' role line). Those four are merged into utils/sanitizePrompt.ts FIRST, which is why this is a consolidation rather than a removal. THE LIVE DEFECT IT EXPOSED: two exported functions were both named sanitizePrompt with different semantics, and server/ai/executive.ts — Pax's chat engine, both chat paths — had imported the weaker one, sanitizing org knowledge files and Pax project files with it and concatenating the result into the SYSTEM role message with NO <<USER_DATA>> envelope, although Pax's system prompt only instructs the model about that envelope. Uploaded document text carrying <|im_start|>, </system>, [INST], 'disregard the above rules' or 'override your system instructions' reached the system prompt intact. A FOURTH copy was found while writing the guard test: server/utils/injectionRateLimiter.ts held a hand-copied SUBSET (9 markers vs 15, 10 phrases vs 20) beneath a header claiming it used 'the same regex set used by sanitizePrompt' — so probes the sanitizer redacted never incremented ai_injection_attempts, making a founder-visible count a systematic undercount. It now delegates to detectInjectionPatterns(). Verified non-regression rather than asserted: the pre-existing promptInjection.test.ts (24 attacks + 14 legitimate inputs, written against the middleware's own list) passes unchanged through the delegating middleware, and singleInjectionSanitizer.test.ts runs a 35-attack corpus plus a 10-string benign corpus so the coverage gain and its cost sit in the same file. 2026-08-14, THE OPACITY RULE IS NARROWED — unreachedExports 580 -> 1439 and opaqueExports 984 -> 125. THIS IS THE ONE RAISE THIS RATCHET RESERVES TO SIGN-OFF, AND IT HAS IT: founder approval, picker, 2026-08-14 ('Approve the narrowing'). Nothing regressed and no code was deleted or added — the gate simply stopped exempting exports it never needed to exempt. WHAT CHANGED: a DESTRUCTURING dynamic import no longer makes a module opaque. `const { routeAITask } = await import('./x')` binds a bare identifier the usage tokeniser already sees, so exempting the module's OTHER exports on the strength of it was pure loss — that is how aiRouter.ts shielded ten exports occurring nowhere else in production because three siblings were destructured out of it. Of 1,244 distinct dynamic-import specifiers, 838 were reached ONLY by destructuring and 27 ever took a namespace binding, which is why 859 exports move in one step. A namespace binding, a `(await import(...)).default`, and a bare side-effect import ALL still confer opacity: this linter's bias is that a false OPAQUE is a miss while a false UNREACHED is an ACCUSATION, so anything not clearly destructured keeps its exemption. A TRAP CAUGHT DURING THE CHANGE, worth recording: the first implementation skipped destructured imports entirely, which also removed them from importedModules — and moduleOrphans jumped 45 -> 217, i.e. 172 modules that ARE imported were about to be reported as 'nothing imports this file at all'. A false accusation at scale. The two questions are now separate: EVERY dynamic import still marks the module imported (the module-orphan question), and only a non-destructured one marks it opaque (the symbol-exemption question). moduleOrphans is unchanged at 45, which is the check that the split is right. [CORRECTED, unit 117 wave audit: this note previously claimed the reclaimed exports included achMandateSetup/achAutopay symbols 'which its opacity rule had been hiding' — FALSE.
